hero.title: Cook Senegal. <accent>Share</accent> its Teranga.
hero.subtitle: A hands-on workshop around thiéboudiène, Senegal's national dish: discover the ingredients, cook together, then gather around the shared bowl — the way families do.
hero.caption: Thiéboudiène Workshop · Dakar

intro.statement: In Wolof, “Kër” means <accent>home</accent> and “Téranga” means hospitality. Here you are not a spectator: you are welcomed like family and invited to roll up your sleeves.

handsOn.title: Hands-on workshop
handsOn.text: We cook together, from start to finish

teranga.title: Hospitality as a way of life
teranga.text1: In Senegal, no one eats alone. The dish is set in the middle of the table, everyone gathers around the bowl, and the guest is always served first. That is Teranga: an everyday generosity that turns a stranger into family.
teranga.text2: Our workshops carry that tradition forward. You leave with a recipe — and, above all, with the feeling of having been welcomed into someone's home.

workshop.lead: Thiéboudiène — “rice and fish” in Wolof — is the dish of celebrations and family lunches alike. Since 2021, the art of preparing it has been inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. With us, you cook it with your own hands.

ingredients.title: The ingredients
ingredients.text: Fish, rice, vegetables and spices: learn to recognise and choose them.

gestures.title: The techniques
gestures.text: Prepare, season, cook: the gestures and secrets handed down by the founder.

history.title: The story
history.text: A presentation on screen tells where the dish comes from and its place in Senegalese life.

sharing.title: The sharing
sharing.text: Everyone gathers around the communal bowl to enjoy what you cooked together.

founder.title: A host and a keeper of culture
founder.text: An ambassador of Senegalese cuisine, the founder of Kër Téranga hosts every workshop and shares the recipes, gestures and stories behind thiéboudiène.

journey.title: The journey of a dish
journey.text: Four moments, one table: each workshop follows thiéboudiène from the stalls of Dakar to the moment everyone shares the meal.

market.title: The market
market.text: The colours and scents of the fresh produce that give the dish its taste.

prep.title: Preparation
prep.text: Peel, chop, season: everyone finds their place in the kitchen.

cook.title: Cooking
cook.text: The slow simmer that gives the rice all its flavour.

share.title: Sharing
share.text: The dish set in the middle — and the conversation begins.

about.title: A home, a culture, a way of welcoming

name.terangaText: Senegalese hospitality, a founding value made of generosity, sharing and respect for others.
name.together: Kër Téranga means "the house of hospitality": a place where every visitor is welcomed like family.

heritage.title: A dish recognised by UNESCO
heritage.text1: Born in the fishing communities of Saint-Louis, ceebu jën — often spelled thiéboudiène — became Senegal's national dish. Its recipe and techniques are traditionally handed down from mother to daughter, and it is shared from one large communal bowl, often eaten by hand.
heritage.text2: In December 2021, UNESCO inscribed “Ceebu jën, a culinary art of Senegal” on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity — recognising a dish that is also an affirmation of Senegalese identity.
